title: Digital Rights and Responsibilities
tagline: Protect your data, be respectful, and check before you share.
description: Digital citizenship is about using phones and the internet safely and responsibly — protecting your personal data, treating others with respect, and checking information before you pass it on.
outcomes: Protect your personal data and privacy
Check information before you share it
Recognise your responsibilities as a digital citizen

lessons.title: Your data and privacy
lessons.body:
Your personal information has value. Protecting it keeps you safe.

## What to protect
Your NRC number, PINs and passwords, your home details and photos. Do not share these with people you do not trust, and never enter them on a link you did not expect.

## Simple habits
Use a screen lock. Do not reuse one password everywhere. Think before you allow an app to see your contacts, photos or location.
key_points: Protect your NRC number, PINs and passwords
Do not share private details with strangers
Use a screen lock and strong passwords
Think before apps access your data
lessons.try_it: Check the screen lock on your phone and change one weak password.

lessons.title: Being respectful online
lessons.body:
How you treat others online matters as much as in person.

## Communicate well
Be polite, even in disagreement. Do not share private messages or photos of others without permission. Words online can spread far and last a long time.

## Report harm
If you see bullying, threats or scams, do not pass them on. Report them on the platform and talk to someone you trust.
key_points: Be polite, even when you disagree
Do not share others' private messages or photos
Online words spread far and last
lessons.try_it: Think of one way you can make a group chat you are in kinder.

lessons.title: Scenario: Should you share it?
lessons.body: A dramatic message arrives on your phone and asks you to forward it to everyone. Work through what to do.
key_points: Checking first protects you and others
The feedback explains the safest choice

scenario.prompt: A message says a local clinic is giving free money today and tells you to forward it to ten people. What do you do?
options: Forward it quickly so friends do not miss out
Pause and check whether it is true before sharing
Forward it and add that it must be true
feedback: Forwarding fast is how false messages and scams spread.
Right — checking first protects you and the people you would send it to.
Adding your name makes others trust a message you have not checked.

options: Ask the clinic or a trusted official, or look for an official notice
Count how many people already shared it
Trust it because a friend sent it
feedback: Yes — go to the source or an official channel to confirm.
Many shares does not make something true.
Even trusted friends forward things they have not checked.

quiz.question: Which of these should you keep private?
options: Your PINs, passwords and NRC number
quiz.explanation: Keep PINs, passwords, your NRC number and personal details private and safe.

quiz.question: Before forwarding a dramatic message, you should:
options: Check if it is true first
quiz.explanation: Check whether a message is true before you share it, so you do not spread false information.
